transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-29 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~57m
Attendees: Sanjay Rao (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Elena Park (Redwood CSM); Lena Ortiz (CTO, Monarch Health), Marcus Bell (Lead Eng), Priya Singh (Product), Omar Reyes (Infra), Jules (SRE)

Summary: weekly POC sync to review integration progress for application-level SDK usage (tool/function calling), structured output for patient-summary use case, and next steps for performance tests and security docs. A few SDK edge cases and streaming semantics discussed.

Topics: integration status, streaming vs non-streaming tool calls, structured output schema, error handling and retry/backoff, telemetry and trace IDs, latency/cost tradeoffs, dedicated capacity discussion, security/KMS and audit logs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sanjay: hey everyone, thanks for joining i think we have about 45 to 60 minutes today, quick roll call?
[00:08] Lena: hi lena here, sorry i'm juggling a couple things - marcus and priya are on as well.
[00:12] Marcus: yep here, morning.
[00:14] Priya: hi all.
[00:16] Maya: maya here from redwood, i'll do the SDK deep parts.
[00:19] Elena: elena on CSM side.
[00:21] Sanjay: great, so quick agenda: 1) where integration is at, 2) review a couple of failing cases in structured output mapping, 3) streaming tool calls and retry behavior, 4) next steps and perf test scheduling. sound ok?
[00:30] Lena: yes sounds good.

[00:35] Marcus: quick status - we've got the basic SDK hooked into our backend, calling the hosted endpoint for generation. We implemented the function call emulation using the SDK's tool-call wrapper, but we've seen a couple of cases where the model returns free text instead of the structured patient-summary JSON.
[00:48] Maya: yeah that's the thing we wanted to look at - most times the structured schema is respected but when prompt context gets long or there are interrupted tokens we see hallucinated fields or trailing narrative. do you have an example?
[00:59] Marcus: yes i dropped one in the shared drive - file name: monarch-patient-summary-failure-20260727.log, the output contains stray phrases like "recommended follow up" outside the json block, and occasionally the SDK's parser fails because the model returned a top-level string then json.
[01:16] Sanjay: that's pretty common when the model sees ambiguous instruction. two routes: 1) stricter system prompt and output validators, or 2) use SDK's structured_output parameter with enforced schema which returns an object or an explicit error token. Maya, can you talk through how the SDK handles this today?
[01:32] Maya: sure - so the SDK has both a post-processing parser and an option for model-side enforcement. post-process we run a fast regex and attempt to parse the first JSON-looking block; that is what you're seeing fail when leading narrative appears. the newer flow is to enable structured_output:true in the request which instructs our serving runtime to prefer the structured output codec — it will return a structured payload or an explicit failure reason. caveat: older open models can still emit free text, so we fallback to the parser. also note there's a small latency tax (~50-120ms) depending on model and sequence length.
[02:08] Jules: is that the same as the tool call path? like when we call an external tool to fetch patient records?
[02:12] Maya: related but separate. tool/function calling is implemented as an explicit token exchange pattern. you declare tools in the request, model can respond with a tool call object which the SDK catches and invokes the designated function. we stream events for tool-activity if streaming enabled - so you can show partial tool-call payloads in the UI. structured_output is orthogonal, it controls the final output serialization.
[02:33] Priya: we were also hoping to have the model populate a predefined FHIR-lite structure for our patient-summary, a list of meds, allergies, last-visit date, and a short prioritized plan. can we map structured_output to that?
[02:43] Maya: yes - we can accept a JSON schema (or example) and the SDK will attempt to coerce outputs into that shape. best practice is to provide an example plus a small set of unit tests - we have a small harness that can run prompt+response checks and flag regressions.
[02:56] Marcus: what's the behavior on partial outputs during streaming? we need the UI to render incremental fields as they arrive, but not show incomplete json that breaks the client.
[03:05] Maya: for streaming tool calls we emit chunked events: meta tokens, then tool-call begin, tool-call payload chunks, tool-call end, then final structured object. We include event types so client can decide to render a placeholder until final structured object arrives. if you want incremental field updates we can send delta objects but that requires more parsing on client side. also we expose a "structured_fragment" event so the UI can safely show validated fields as they pass schema checks.
[03:30] Omar: oh interesting, that structured_fragment event - is that enabled by default or opt-in?
[03:34] Maya: opt-in per-route. you enable streaming:true and structured_fragments:true. we usually recommend opt-in for prototypes since it increases message volume.
[03:44] Lena: security question - when tool calls fetch PHI do we hit Redwood logs or is that under our own VPC/private deployment?
[03:51] Sanjay: good call - currently you're on hosted trial so logs and content go through Redwood's control plane; we offer encryption at rest and in transit, but for regulated PHI we recommend Private deployment (VPC or on-prem). in Private mode the payloads stay in your VPC and our control plane only transfers non-sensitive telemetry. we also support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and audit logs.
[04:16] Lena: what's the effort to run Private? Marcus how much infra overhead?
[04:20] Marcus: we did some initial runs, seems like a week to set up networking and IAM, another week to validate. but we need Redwood's ops docs and a small install script.
[04:30] Sanjay: we'll share the Private deployment runbook and an OSS-like quickstart. expected timeline for pilot customers is 2-3 weeks for VPC integration if you're able to allocate infra resources.
[04:40] Priya: related: compliance - SOC2 and data retention. do you have a short doc we can show security?
[04:45] Elena: i'll send the SOC2 summary and the KMS integration guide after this call. also a short checklist for the security review.
[04:52] Marcus: great. back to perf: we've noticed p95 latency spikes when sequence length exceeds 1k tokens and concurrent users hit ~30.
[05:00] Maya: yep that's expected - kernel selection and KV cache behavior changes; for long-context workloads we recommend either a) dedicated pool with higher memory GPUs or b) prefix caching for repeated chunks. if you expect many concurrent short requests, dedicated with batching is usually more cost-effective. we can also recommend quantization profiles which help memory footprint but may slightly impact output quality.
[05:25] Jules: did you see improvement when we switched the model to the smaller rdx-2-3b variant?
[05:29] Maya: yes lower model size reduced latency and cost but you lose some instruction-following fidelity. for structured outputs rdx-2 is fine if you have strong validation in post-processing.
[05:39] Marcus: ok for the POC we're fine with hosted rdx-2 but if we go to production we'll want dedicated.
[05:44] Sanjay: noted. we'll send pricing for dedicated tiers for your usage estimate.

[05:50] -- Demo/Walkthrough --
[05:52] Maya: i'll share my screen — here is the SDK call pattern we're using: initialize client with apiKey, create route with streaming:true, tools:[patient_db_fetch], structured_output:{schema:...}. example code in node: (handwave) redwood.client.call({model, route, prompt, tools, streaming:true}) then attach on('event') for tool-calls.
[06:10] Priya: can you paste the node snippet into chat?
[06:12] Maya: done - also in the shared drive under redwood/sdk-examples/monarch. note the retry/backoff strategy: we recommend idempotent tool-ids and a 3x exponential backoff with jitter.
[06:24] Marcus: we saw an edge case where a tool-call returned a 502 from our internal service and the SDK retried three times, which caused duplicate writes in our logs. how do you recommend avoiding that?
[06:34] Maya: we support idempotency tokens on tool calls; pass a unique call_id per logical operation. the SDK will surface retry events and you can filter duplicates on your side or use our at-most-once invocation mode with acknowledgement tokens.
[06:48] Omar: about observability — can we get token-level traces tied to our request IDs?
[06:52] Elena: yes we can pass your trace id header X-Trace-ID and we'll correlate latency and token counts in the console; we'll also share a sample dashboard for the POC.
[06:59] Marcus: perfect. also can we limit model fallbacks? i don't want automatic downgrade to smaller models during testing.
[07:06] Sanjay: you can pin model version per route and set fallback policies to none. currently your route allows auto-fallback to conserve cost. we'll put that on the change list.

[07:14] Priya: one more question about structured output failure modes - how do we handle partial schema mismatch? say meds field is missing but others ok.
[07:22] Maya: you can define required fields in the schema. the SDK will either return a validation error or attempt to coerce. we recommend returning a structured response with error metadata so UI can show "partial" view and surface missing items for manual review.
[07:36] Lena: ok that helps. are there recommended tests we should run to detect regressions?
[07:40] Maya: yes our eval harness can run unit prompts and compare extraction metrics (precision/recall on fields). we'll share the harness and a small seed set you can expand.

[07:50] Sanjay: quick commercial note - for projected 100k tokens/month the hosted plan is cheaper up to a point but Dedicated begins to make sense once steady throughput and latency SLOs are important. i'll send a delta.
[08:02] Lena: thanks.

[08:05] -- Wrap / Recap --
[08:06] Sanjay: recap: Maya will share SDK snippet + streaming example + structured_fragment sample; Elena will share SOC2 doc and KMS note; Marcus/Jules will run integration tests and provide logs; Sanjay will send pricing and Private runbook. we'll schedule the perf benchmark (50 concurrent) w/ dedicated option week of 2026-08-10.
[08:25] Lena: sounds good. one ask: can you include a small security blurb for our legal review?
[08:30] Elena: will do - short 1-pager and links.
[08:33] Priya: thanks everyone.
[08:35] Sanjay: thanks all, we'll follow up in doc and slack. bye.

End of transcript.
